Evolutionof Engine

An immersive experience for the Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum, Bengaluru, where visitors explore, assemble and test engines instead of reading about them.

Project by Raj, Poorvesh, Akhil & Saumya

Seeing an engine isn’t understanding one.

The problem

Traditional exhibits rely on static displays and information panels, which make complex mechanical ideas hard for young visitors to grasp. There’s a gap between observing an engine and experiencing how it works.

The brief

Design an immersive experience at VITM that turns engine exploration into interactive learning. With 3D visualisation, panoramic projection, spatial audio and haptic feedback, visitors explore engine mechanics, discover where engines are used, and test them on a simulated track.

A booth where engines come alive.

A gesture-controlled space combining 3D visuals, spatial audio and a haptic floor, so mechanical learning becomes something you do, hear and feel.

  • Explore engines in 3D, from every angle.
  • Understand what happens inside through animated cross-sections.
  • Connect each engine to the vehicles it powers.
  • Experiment by installing engines into different vehicles.
  • Test their performance on a simulated track.
  • Feel and hear each engine’s sound and thump through a vibrating floor.

A cylindrical booth, 3–5 m across and 3.05 m tall, with projection, 5.1 surround sound and a haptic floor.

Pitched to the VITM curators on 3 Nov 2026. The feedback was positive, and the museum is keen to develop it further.
